introduction.body: Assess how well your business attracts new employees, supports existing staff and creates a workplace where people want to stay.

questions.label: Do you have a recruitment plan to attract the people your business needs now and in the future?
questions.helpText: Planning ahead makes it easier to recruit the right people when new work or business opportunities arise.

positiveMessage.title: Recruitment Ready!
positiveMessage.body: Your Strength: You are proactively planning workforce attraction and recruitment activities to support future projects, business goals and staffing needs.

recommendation.title: Develop a Recruitment Plan
recommendation.body:
Opportunity to Improve: Develop a recruitment plan that matches your future projects, business goals and staffing needs.

Consider:

  • Identifying future staffing needs
  • Planning for hard-to-fill roles
  • Building relationships with schools, training providers and employment services
  • Exploring alternative workforce options where shortages exist

Learn more about interviewing and recruiting.

Explore recruitment support through:

  • Territory WorkerConnect to promote the job opportunities available and directly connect with suitable jobseekers
  • Workforce Australia for free recruitment assistance
  • Recruitment agencies for specialist recruitment support

questions.label: Have you identified occupations or roles that may be difficult to recruit for?
questions.helpText: Hard-to-fill roles can delay projects, increase costs and place extra pressure on your existing workforce.

positiveMessage.title: Market Aware!
positiveMessage.body: Your Strength: You understand workforce market pressures and can plan accordingly.

recommendation.title: Identify Recruitment Challenges
recommendation.body:
Opportunity to Improve: Identify the roles that are difficult to recruit now or may become difficult to fill in the future.

Understanding workforce shortages early gives you more time to recruit, train and build future workforce pipelines.

Review labour market information and industry trends to understand where shortages may affect your business.

Learn more about interviewing and recruiting.

If shortages are identified, consider:

  • Apprenticeships or Traineeships
  • Territory WorkerConnect to promote the job opportunities available and directly connect with suitable jobseekers
  • Skilled migration pathways where workforce shortages persist
  • Workforce Australia to connect with jobseekers
  • Connecting with skilled veterans through the Veteran Employment Program
  • Connecting with ISACNT to better understand industry workforce challenges and available workforce solutions, which may result in the occupation being listed on the NT Skilled Occupation Priority List (NTSOPL), which can influence policy, funding and increase focus on emerging skill needs

Seek advice from a Territory Business Advisor to identify workforce support programs and workforce development opportunities.

questions.label: Does your business create a workplace where people want to stay?
questions.helpText: Employee retention is influenced by workplace culture, leadership, wellbeing, communication, flexibility and opportunities to learn and grow.

positiveMessage.title: Positive Employee Experience!
positiveMessage.body: Your Strength: You have workplace practices that support employee wellbeing, engagement and retention. You regularly seek employee feedback and use it to improve the workplace.

recommendation.title: Improve Employee Experience
recommendation.body:
Opportunity to Improve: Think about what helps people enjoy working for your business and encourages them to stay.

Consider:

  • Good leadership
  • Regular communication
  • Employee recognition
  • Career development
  • Flexible work arrangements
  • Wellbeing and mental health support
  • Managing psychosocial risks such as high workloads, fatigue, bullying or workplace conflict

Learn more about flexible working arrangements or exit interviews.

questions.label: Have you considered workforce accommodation, transport and travel requirements for regional or remote projects?
questions.helpText: For regional and remote work, accommodation, transport and travel can affect your ability to attract and retain workers.

positiveMessage.title: Logistics Ready!
positiveMessage.body: Your Strength: You understand the workforce and operational challenges associated with regional and remote project delivery.

recommendation.title: Plan Accommodation & Logistics
recommendation.body:
Opportunity to Improve: Plan accommodation, travel and transport early when preparing for regional or remote projects.

Consider:

  • Accommodation availability
  • Travel arrangements
  • Roster design
  • Mobilisation planning
  • Employee wellbeing

Planning ahead can improve recruitment, retention and project delivery.

Learn more about remote and isolated work.

questions.label: Does your business actively support workforce diversity and inclusive employment practices?
questions.helpText: Diverse and inclusive workplaces help businesses attract more people, improve innovation and build stronger teams.

positiveMessage.title: Inclusive Workplace!
positiveMessage.body: Your Strength: You are creating a more inclusive and sustainable workforce.

recommendation.title: Strengthen Diversity & Inclusion
recommendation.body:
Opportunity to Improve: Review your recruitment and employment practices to make sure everyone has the opportunity to succeed.

Creating an inclusive workplace can help you attract a wider range of people, improve employee engagement and strengthen workplace culture.

Learn more about inclusive employment practices.

conclusion.body:
Well done in completing this attraction and retention questionnaire.

Download or save your results. Use them to inform your Workforce Action Plan and strengthen your workforce readiness!
